newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks end tad higher in token volume.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks end tad higher in token volume.

text.p: Argentine leading stocks ended fractionally higher Monday in dismal volume and were seen volatile Tuesday when the key U.S. Employment Cost Index will be unveiled, dealers said.

"Absolutely nothing happened today -- nobody wants to take any chances ahead of a battery of U.S. economic data starting Tuesday which will allow us to predict movements in interest rates," said Miguel Daneri at brokers Boston Securities.
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV edged up 0.1 percent to 716.51 while floor volume trickled down to 9.7 million pesos from Friday's already extremely weak tally of 12.7 million.
Floor volume also dwindled to 41.2 million pesos from 79.5 million Friday.

"You can write today off, and maybe also tomorrow and even Wednesday because the (May Day) holiday Thursday and the anxiety building up towards Friday's U.S. jobs report has sent everyone away," another dealer said.
But he did not not rule out a moderate selling or buying drive if the Employment Cost Index came in above or below the consensus estimate of 0.8 percent Tuesday.
The broad market dipped 0.2 percent, with winners edging out losers 18 to 14 and 21 issues closing flat.
Best main-tier performers were footwear and textile firm Alpargatas, steelmaker Acindar and foods giant Molinos, which advanced 2.4 percent, 1.9 percent and 1.7 percent, respectively.
MerVal losers were led by holding company Comercial del Plata, which dropped 1.7 percent, steelmaker Siderca, off 1.2 percent, and carmaker Ciadea and oil giant YPF, both down 0.9 percent.
